description:
The second arm of the blank-field chain, app/cbl/COSGN00C.cbl:123-127, driven with a user id the file actually holds. USERIDI carries ADMIN004 - the fourth seeded row, zero-based row 3 - so the test at :118 is false and the ordered EVALUATE TRUE of :117 falls through to WHEN PASSWDI OF COSGN0AI = SPACES OR LOW-VALUES at :123, which matches because the password arrives as eight spaces. :124 moves 'Y' into WS-ERR-FLG, :125 moves 'Please enter Password ...' into WS-MESSAGE, :126 moves -1 into PASSWDL rather than USERIDL - the whole of the difference in cursor placement between the two arms, and the one thing that still distinguishes them once the message has been truncated to the screen's width - and :127 performs SEND-SIGNON-SCREEN. Typing a key the file holds is deliberate: it means this case cannot be mistaken for the not-found arm at :247-251, because the key typed here would have been found had anything looked for it. This arm is reachable only because the earlier one did not match, so the case reads the ordering of :117-130 from the second position; case06 reads it from the first.

What :132-136 do on a rejected path, and the read that does not happen. Those lines sit after END-EVALUATE at :130 and outside every arm of it, so they run unconditionally: CDEMO-USER-ID receives FUNCTION UPPER-CASE(USERIDI) and therefore carries ADMIN004 - a real, non-blank value on a rejected sign-on - while WS-USER-PWD receives FUNCTION UPPER-CASE of eight spaces, which is eight spaces, because a space has no case. Only then does :138 test the flag, find it on, and skip READ-USER-SEC-FILE. USRSEC is therefore read exactly zero times, which is stated here positively rather than left to be inferred from an absence: all ten rows are seeded, every one of them stays unread, no SEC-USR-* value appears anywhere in the outcome because no record was ever returned, and the expectedFinalState images are the seeded rows unchanged. That is the sharpest point of this case. A translation that looked ADMIN004 up because it had a valid key to hand would paint exactly the right screen and would satisfy every other expectation declared here; the COBOL does not look it up, because :138 has already been decided by :124. For the same reason CDEMO-USER-TYPE stays blank - it is written only at :227, on the path where :223 compared the passwords equal - and it must not read 'A' merely because ADMIN004 happens to be an admin in the seed data. CDEMO-FROM-TRANID, CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM and CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT are written at :224-228 on that same path and are likewise untouched here.

The screen. This path never executes MOVE LOW-VALUES TO COSGN0AO - that is :81, on the cold start where EIBCALEN is zero - and app/cpy-bms/COSGN00.CPY:85 declares 01 COSGN0AO REDEFINES COSGN0AI, where each field's input view spends xxxL plus xxxF plus a four-byte FILLER, seven bytes, exactly where the output view spends a three-byte FILLER plus xxxC, xxxP, xxxH and xxxV. xxxI and xxxO are therefore the same bytes at the same width, so what RECEIVE MAP left there is what SEND MAP transmits: USERIDO is ADMIN004 and PASSWDO is the eight spaces that were typed. ERRMSGO is 'Please enter Password ...', twenty-five characters - one more than the twenty-four of the user-id message, which is why the two cannot be told apart by length alone - right-padded to the PIC X(78) that app/cpy-bms/COSGN00.CPY:152 declares, the width at which the 80-byte WS-MESSAGE of :38 loses its last two bytes. Two absences are worth stating rather than leaving to be rediscovered. :59 reads *COPY DFHATTR., an asterisk in column 7 and so a COBOL comment, which means no DFHATTR attribute constant applies to this program at all. And COSGN00C never copies CSSETATY, so there is no DFHRED-plus-'*' emphasis applied at run time: the error is emphasised by the PASSWDL cursor request together with ERRMSG's static COLOR=RED and ATTRB=(ASKIP,BRT,FSET) at app/bms/COSGN00.bms:197-200. Note also that PASSWD is statically ATTRB=(DRK,FSET,UNPROT) at app/bms/COSGN00.bms:175-180 - a dark, non-display field - which is a property of the map and not something the program sets, and which is why the eight spaces travel back in a field the terminal never shows.

USRSEC is seeded from app/jcl/DUSRSECJ.jcl:35-44, whose ten in-stream rows are 57 characters where app/cpy/CSUSR01Y.cpy declares 80: SEC-USR-ID X(08) at 0, SEC-USR-FNAME X(20) at 8, SEC-USR-LNAME X(20) at 28, SEC-USR-PWD X(08) at 48, SEC-USR-TYPE X(01) at 56 - which is 57 - then SEC-USR-FILLER X(23) at 57, which is 80. The 23-byte shortfall is supplied once at seed time by the declared USRSEC_FILLER_PAD_57_TO_80 normalisation and never hand-padded, and the 80-character expectedFinalState images prove that span was emitted as 23 spaces - a record missing it would be short by exactly 23. The same job corroborates the target width twice, with DCB=(LRECL=80,RECFM=FB) on SYSUT2 and RECORDSIZE(80,80) KEYS(8,0) on the cluster. The dataset is addressed by its binding key USRSEC - the CICS file name at :39 - and never by a dataset name. expectedWrites is empty as a positive assertion: COSGN00C contains no WRITE, REWRITE or DELETE on any path, and the read at :211-219 does not even specify UPDATE, so it takes no lock and holds no record. expectedReturnCode is 0 because grep -c RETURN-CODE over the program is 0.

Determinism and the two substitutions. POPULATE-HEADER-INFO opens with MOVE FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE TO WS-CURDATE-DATA at :179, so the clock is pinned rather than read: 2022-07-19T23:12:33, traceable to this program's own version footer at :259 and expressed as a fixed local date-time so no timezone can shift it. Through app/cpy/CSDAT01Y.cpy, WS-CURDATE-MM-DD-YY is MM '/' DD '/' YY with YY taken from WS-CURDATE-YEAR(3:2), giving CURDATEO exactly 07/19/22 at its PIC X(8); WS-CURTIME-HH-MM-SS is HH ':' MM ':' SS, eight bytes, moved into CURTIMEO which app/cpy-bms/COSGN00.CPY:122 declares PIC X(9) - hence 23:12:33 followed by exactly one trailing space. Note that width: the sibling COUSR02 map declares its CURTIMEO PIC X(8) and the two must not be conflated. APPLID and SYSID come from EXEC CICS ASSIGN at :198-204, which has no Java equivalent and which neither application.yml nor application-test.yml binds, so CICSAWS1 and AWS1 space-padded to PIC X(8) are pinned constants standing in for those two calls; all twenty cases use the same pair, and the substitution is stated rather than hidden.

Provenance. Every expected value above is statically derived - by structured reading of app/cbl/COSGN00C.cbl cross-checked against app/cpy/CSUSR01Y.cpy for the record layout, app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy for the communication area, app/cpy/COTTL01Y.cpy and app/cpy/CSMSG01Y.cpy and app/cpy/CSDAT01Y.cpy for the literals and the header, app/cpy-bms/COSGN00.CPY with app/bms/COSGN00.bms for the screen field shapes, app/csd/CARDDEMO.CSD for transaction CC00, and app/jcl/DUSRSECJ.jcl:35-44 for the ten seed rows. It was never captured from a live COBOL execution, which is empirically impossible in this environment: there is no z/OS or CICS runtime, the available compiler reports its indexed file handler disabled, no Language Environment CEE* services exist, and DFHAID, DFHBMSCA and DFHATTR are absent from the repository. Only the provenance of the expected values is substituted; the twenty cases, the field-for-field diffing and the diff-count-equals-zero gate all stand.

The unit is SignOnService, driven as a plain object with a fixture-backed SecUserRepository, and the eleven-field screen is projected by SignOnController, also a plain object - no MockMvc, no HTTP, no servlet container and no JobLauncher in the path. All conversation state travels in the payload, so no server-side session exists to hold any of it. The password stays plaintext because app/cbl/COSGN00C.cbl:223 compares it in plaintext; that is an inherited property of the legacy design and an explicit non-goal of this migration, not something to correct here. Neither the backward-GO TO restructuring gate nor the abend gate applies: grep -c "GO TO" and grep -c CEE3ABD over app/cbl/COSGN00C.cbl are both 0, and neither is faked.
